neural-nets.prompt: Why does a network need nonlinear activation functions?
neural-nets.explanation: W2(W1x)=(W2W1)x\mathbf W_2(\mathbf W_1\mathbf x)=(\mathbf W_2\mathbf W_1)\mathbf xW2​(W1​x)=(W2​W1​)x: depth adds nothing without nonlinearity.
options: Without them, stacked layers collapse into a single linear map
They reduce the number of parameters

neural-nets.prompt: What is the maximum value of the sigmoid's derivative?
neural-nets.explanation: σ′(z)=σ(1−σ)\sigma'(z)=\sigma(1-\sigma)σ′(z)=σ(1−σ) peaks at 0.25 when z=0z=0z=0, one reason sigmoids cause vanishing gradients in deep stacks.

neural-nets.prompt: Which activation is the standard choice inside Transformer feed-forward layers like BERT and GPT?
neural-nets.explanation: GELU is a smooth ReLU-like function; many recent LLMs use SwiGLU.

neural-nets.prompt: The universal approximation theorem guarantees that gradient descent will find a good network.
neural-nets.explanation: It only says a good enough network exists, not that training finds it or that it generalizes.

backprop.prompt: In z=Wh+b\mathbf z=\mathbf W\mathbf h+\mathbf bz=Wh+b with δ=∂L/∂z\boldsymbol\delta=\partial\mathcal L/\partial\mathbf zδ=∂L/∂z, what is ∂L/∂h\partial\mathcal L/\partial\mathbf h∂L/∂h?
backprop.explanation: The error signal flows back through the transposed weights.

backprop.prompt: How is the error signal passed back through a ReLU?
backprop.explanation: ReLU's derivative is 1 where the input was positive and 0 elsewhere.
options: Multiplied element-wise by 1[z>0]\mathbb 1[\mathbf z\gt0]1[z>0]
Multiplied by z\mathbf zz

backprop.prompt: On the graph f=(x⋅y)+zf=(x\cdot y)+zf=(x⋅y)+z with x=2,y=−3,z=4x=2, y=-3, z=4x=2,y=−3,z=4, what is ∂f/∂x\partial f/\partial x∂f/∂x?
backprop.explanation: ∂f/∂x=y=−3\partial f/\partial x=y=-3∂f/∂x=y=−3.

backprop.prompt: Why is reverse-mode differentiation used for training rather than forward mode?
backprop.explanation: Forward mode would need one pass per parameter; with millions of parameters that is hopeless.
options: One backward pass gives the derivative of a scalar loss with respect to all parameters

training-deep.prompt: What weight variance does He initialization use for ReLU layers?
training-deep.explanation: The factor 2 compensates for ReLU zeroing about half of its inputs.
options: 1/nin1/n_{in}1/nin​
2/nin2/n_{in}2/nin​
2/(nin+nout)2/(n_{in}+n_{out})2/(nin​+nout​)

training-deep.prompt: For 10 balanced classes, roughly what should the initial cross-entropy loss be? (natural log)
training-deep.explanation: A model that predicts uniformly gives ln⁡10≈2.30\ln 10\approx2.30ln10≈2.30. A very different value hints at a bug.

training-deep.prompt: Which normalization layer normalizes across features within each example and is standard in Transformers?
training-deep.explanation: It does not depend on batch statistics, so it works with any batch size and sequence length.

training-deep.prompt: Which are good first steps when a new model won't train? (select all)
training-deep.explanation: Regularization comes after the model can fit at all.
options: Sweep the learning rate on a log scale

pytorch-loop.prompt: Which line must come between loss.backward() and the next forward pass to apply the update?
pytorch-loop.explanation: step() updates the parameters using the computed gradients.
Clipping prevents a single huge gradient from destabilizing training.
options: Rescales the gradient if its global norm exceeds 1.0

pytorch-loop.prompt: You should apply softmax to the model output before passing it to F.cross_entropy.
pytorch-loop.explanation: F.cross_entropy takes raw logits and applies a stable log-softmax itself.

cnn.prompt: Input 224×224×3, a convolution with 64 filters of 7×7, stride 2 and padding 3. What is the output height?
cnn.explanation: ⌊(224−7+6)/2⌋+1=112\lfloor(224-7+6)/2\rfloor+1=112⌊(224−7+6)/2⌋+1=112.

cnn.prompt: How many parameters does that convolution have (including biases)?
cnn.explanation: 7⋅7⋅3⋅64+64=9,4727\cdot7\cdot3\cdot64+64=9{,}4727⋅7⋅3⋅64+64=9,472.

cnn.prompt: What is the receptive field of three stacked 3×3 convolutions with stride 1?
Why do residual connections help very deep networks train?
cnn.explanation: ∂y/∂x=∂F/∂x+I\partial\mathbf y/\partial\mathbf x=\partial\mathcal F/\partial\mathbf x+\mathbf I∂y/∂x=∂F/∂x+I, so the gradient never has to pass only through many small factors.
options: The identity path gives gradients a direct route backward
They reduce the number of parameters

rnn.prompt: Why do vanilla RNNs struggle with long-range dependencies?
rnn.explanation: The product of Jacobians behaves like WhhT−t\mathbf W_{hh}^{T-t}WhhT−t​.
options: Gradients through many time steps vanish or explode, like repeated matrix powers
They can only read one word

rnn.prompt: Which mechanism lets an LSTM preserve information over many steps?
rnn.explanation: When the forget gate is near 1, both information and gradients flow through the cell state almost unchanged.
options: The additively updated cell state controlled by a forget gate

rnn.prompt: Gradient clipping fixes exploding gradients but not vanishing ones.
rnn.explanation: Clipping caps large gradients; vanishing needs architectural fixes such as gating, residuals or attention.

transformer.prompt: Why are attention scores divided by dk\sqrt{d_k}dk​​?
transformer.explanation: A dot product of dkd_kdk​ unit-variance terms has variance dkd_kdk​.
options: To keep the variance of the dot products near 1 so the softmax does not saturate

transformer.prompt: What does the causal mask do in a decoder?
transformer.explanation: Setting future scores to −∞-\infty−∞ makes the model a valid next-token predictor.
options: Prevents each token from attending to later tokens

transformer.prompt: How does standard self-attention's time and memory scale with sequence length nnn?
transformer.explanation: The score matrix QK⊤\mathbf Q\mathbf K^\topQK⊤ is n×nn\times nn×n.
options: O(n)O(n)O(n)
O(nlog⁡n)O(n\log n)O(nlogn)
O(n2)O(n^2)O(n2)
O(n3)O(n^3)O(n3)

transformer.prompt: Roughly how many parameters does one Transformer block with model width ddd have (ignoring biases and norms)?
transformer.explanation: About 4d24d^24d2 for the attention projections plus 8d28d^28d2 for a 4× wide feed-forward layer.
options: 4d24d^24d2
8d28d^28d2
12d212d^212d2
d3d^3d3

transformer.prompt: Without positional information, self-attention treats its input as a set.
transformer.explanation: Permuting the tokens permutes the outputs identically, so order must be injected with positional encodings such as RoPE.

gnn.prompt: Why must a GNN's neighbour aggregation be permutation-invariant (sum, mean, max)?
gnn.explanation: The result must not depend on how nodes happen to be numbered.
options: Graph neighbours have no inherent order

gnn.prompt: What is over-smoothing in deep GNNs?
gnn.explanation: Repeated neighbourhood averaging blurs everything together, so most GNNs use only a few layers.
options: Node representations become nearly identical after many rounds of averaging

gnn.prompt: A Transformer can be viewed as a GNN on a fully connected graph of tokens.
gnn.explanation: Attention is message passing with learned weights over every pair of tokens.

ssm.prompt: What is the main advantage of state space models and linear attention over standard attention for long sequences?
ssm.explanation: A fixed-size recurrent state replaces the growing KV cache.
options: Constant memory per generated token and linear scaling in sequence length

ssm.prompt: A linear time-invariant SSM can be trained in parallel because it can be written as…
ssm.explanation: Unrolling the recurrence gives a convolution kernel (CBˉ,CAˉBˉ,… )(\mathbf C\bar{\mathbf B},\mathbf C\bar{\mathbf A}\bar{\mathbf B},\dots)(CBˉ,CAˉBˉ,…).
options: a convolution over the input sequence

ssm.prompt: Why do many long-context models mix a few attention layers into an SSM stack?
ssm.explanation: Attention retrieves precise tokens easily; hybrids combine that with SSM efficiency.
options: Pure SSMs can struggle with exact recall of specific earlier tokens

ssl.prompt: In contrastive learning, what prevents representation collapse?
ssl.explanation: Without negatives or asymmetry, mapping everything to one vector trivially makes views agree.
options: Negative examples (or stop-gradient and momentum-teacher tricks)

ssl.prompt: What do data augmentations define in contrastive learning?
ssl.explanation: Crops, colour jitter and blur teach invariance to exactly those changes.
options: Which differences the representation learns to ignore

ssl.explanation: It measures how linearly accessible useful information is in the representation.
options: Training only a linear classifier on top of frozen features
A probe that measures GPU temperature

compression.prompt: Why does knowledge distillation multiply the KL term by T2T^2T2?
compression.explanation: This keeps the soft and hard losses balanced across temperatures.
options: Softening by temperature TTT scales gradients down by 1/T21/T^21/T2; the factor restores their size

compression.prompt: Which pruning gives real speedups on ordinary GPUs without special sparse kernels?
compression.explanation: Removing whole structures shrinks dense matrix sizes, which standard hardware benefits from.
options: Structured pruning of whole channels, heads or layers

compression.prompt: Quantization-aware training usually recovers more accuracy than post-training quantization at very low bit-widths.
compression.explanation: The model learns to tolerate rounding during training.

__exam.prompt: A 50-layer plain CNN trains worse than a 20-layer one even on the training set. What is the most direct fix?
__exam.explanation: This degradation problem motivated ResNets: identity shortcuts make deeper networks at least as trainable.

__exam.prompt: Count the parameters of a single-head attention layer with d=64d=64d=64 (Q, K, V and output projections, no biases).
__exam.explanation: Four 64×6464\times6464×64 matrices: 4⋅4096=16,3844\cdot4096=16{,}3844⋅4096=16,384.

__exam.prompt: Your loss becomes NaN after a few hundred steps of fp16 training. Which fixes are reasonable? (select all)
__exam.explanation: Instability comes from overflow, underflow and too-large updates.
options: Switch to bf16 or enable dynamic loss scaling
Lower the learning rate and add gradient clipping
Use fused, numerically stable loss functions on logits

__exam.prompt: Which architecture best fits a molecule-toxicity prediction task?
__exam.explanation: Molecules are graphs of atoms and bonds; GNNs respect that structure.
options: A CNN on a fixed grid
A graph neural network with graph-level pooling
A plain RNN over atom names

__exam.prompt: In a Transformer block, the feed-forward layer mixes information across tokens.
__exam.explanation: The FFN processes each token independently; attention is what mixes across tokens.
